## Purpose

Top level proof procedure the GNU Lesser General Public License.

Within the source tree, this unit belongs to `CONTROL`. High-level proof-control layer: preprocessing, saturation loop orchestration, inference scheduling, contraction, SInE, splitting, server/session management, and higher-order inference control.

Authors noted in source headers: Stephan Schulz

### Source-Level Behavior

- `document_processing`: Document processing of the new given clause (depending on the output level).
- `check_ac_status`: Check if the AC theory has been extended by the currently processed clause, and act accordingly.
- `remove_subsumed`: Remove all clauses subsumed by subsumer from set, kill their children. Return number of removed clauses.
- `eliminate_backward_rewritten_clauses`: Remove all processed clauses rewritable with clause and put them into state->tmp_store.
- `eliminate_backward_subsumed_clauses`: Eliminate subsumed processed clauses, return number of clauses deleted.
- `eliminate_unit_simplified_clauses`: Perform unit-back-simplification on the proof state.
- `eliminate_context_sr_clauses`: If required by control, remove all backward-contextual-simplify-reflectable clauses.
- `check_watchlist`: Check if a clause subsumes one or more watchlist clauses, if yes, set appropriate property in clause and remove subsumed clauses.
- `simplify_watchlist`: Simplify all clauses in state->watchlist with processed positive units from state. Assumes that all those clauses are in normal form with respect to all clauses but clause!
- `generate_new_clauses`: Apply the generating inferences to the proof state, putting new clauses into state->tmp_store.
- `eval_clause_set`: Add evaluations to all clauses in state->eval_set. Factored out so that batch-processing with e.g. neural networks can be easily integrated.
- `insert_new_clauses`: Rewrite clauses in state->tmp_store, remove superfluous literals, insert them into state->unprocessed. If an empty clause is detected, return it, otherwise return NULL.
- `replacing_inferences`: Perform the inferences that replace a clause by another: Destructive equality-resolution and/or splitting. Returns NULL if clause was replaced, the empty clause if this produced an empty clause, and the original clause otherwise
- `cleanup_unprocessed_clauses`: Perform maintenenance operations on state->unprocessed, depending on parameters in control: - Remove orphaned clauses - Simplify all unprocessed clauses - Reweigh all unprocessed clauses - Delete "bad" clauses to avoid running out of memories. Simplification can find the empty clause, which is then returned.
- `SATCheck`: Create ground (or pseudo-ground) instances of the clause set, hand them to a SAT solver, and check then for unsatisfiability.
- `print_sharing_factor`: Determine the sharing factor and print it. Potentially expensive, only useful for manual analysis.
- `print_rw_state`: Print the system (R,E,NEW), e.g. the two types of demodulators and the newly generated clauses.
- `ProofControlInit`: Initialize a proof control cell for a given proof state (with at least axioms and signature) and a set of parameters describing the ordering and heuristics.
- `ProofStateResetProcessedSet`: Move all clauses from set into state->unprocessed.
- `ProofStateMoveSetToTmp`: Lightweight version of ProofStateResetProcessedSet which simply moves all clauses from set to tmp_store without reevaluating clause evaluation features.
- `ProofStateResetProcessed`: Move all clauses from the processed clause sets to unprocessed.
- `ProofStateMoveToTmpStore`: Move all clauses from the processed clause sets to tmp store.
- `fvi_param_init`: Initialize the parameters for all feature vector indices in state.
- `ProofStateInit`: Given a proof state with axioms and a heuristic parameter description, initialize the ProofStateCell, i.e. generate the HCB, the ordering, and evaluate the axioms and put them in the unprocessed list.
- `ProcessClause`: Select an unprocessed clause, process it. Return pointer to empty clause if it can be derived, NULL otherwise. This is the core of the main proof procedure.
- `Saturate`: Process clauses until either the empty clause has been derived, a specified number of clauses has been processed, or the clause set is saturated. Return empty clause (if found) or NULL.

### Change Later

- `ProofControlInit` mutates both the caller's heuristic-definition stack and the caller's heuristic parameter object while reconciling direct `heuristic_def` text with stacked `--define-heuristic` options. Rust preserves this in the current compatibility helper, but a later higher-level API could return an initialized control object and normalized parameter snapshot instead of exposing caller-side mutation.
- `ProofControlInit` calls `InitUnifLimits` after writing initialized params back to the caller. In C this stores a process-global pointer to `control->heuristic_parms` for higher-order CSU enumeration rather than deriving new values. Rust stores a safe snapshot of the fields read by the CSU and binding-generation helpers; revisit exact pointer aliasing only if a later port mutates `control->heuristic_parms` after initialization and expects CSU reads to observe those writes.
- In the `FVICollectFeatures` branch, `fvi_param_init` copies the overflow layout fields and assembly-vector length but allocates a fresh assembly vector rather than copying the original vector contents. Rust preserves that shape; revisit only if strategy files or generated specs make non-default assembly vectors observable at this boundary.
- `fvi_param_init` overwrites `cspec->max_symbols` for the active proof-state spec but not for `def_store_cspec`, which keeps the `FVCollectAlloc` default. Rust preserves this difference in the reusable spec helper.
- `fvi_param_init` computes and installs a permutation vector without consulting `control->fvi_parms.use_perm_vectors`; the CLI still records `Direct` versus `Perm` in that field. Rust preserves the initialization path and records the flag for compatibility, but this unused option bit should be revisited once indexed subsumption behavior is covered by end-to-end reference tests.
- The definition-store FV index uses the permutation vector computed from the active proof-state spec rather than from `def_store_cspec`. Rust preserves the effective packing input, but a future cleanup could make this dependency explicit or compute a definition-store-specific vector after compatibility is secured.
- `ProofStateInit` mixes FV-index setup, watchlist indexing, axiom reweighting, initial-clause copying, watchlist matching, derivation pushes, priority rewriting, SOS marking, AC scanning, and global-index reset in one function. Rust now exposes both a C-shaped wrapper for the ported prefix and narrower phase helpers around the same call order; once the remaining side effects are wired, decide whether the public API should keep the C monolith, retain explicit phase helpers, or separate compatibility initialization from reusable proof-state construction.
- `ProofStateInit` also emits its OutputLevel 1 `Initializing proof state` progress line through the process-global `GlobalOut` before performing any initialization work. Rust preserves that timing in the output-capable compatibility wrappers while keeping the plain initializer output-free; exact proof-search and CNF-only file/stdin reference cases pin the banner before AC scanning and before either saturation progress or CNF success output. A later API should report structured initialization events or accept an explicit progress sink instead of coupling state construction to global output.
- The initial-clause path leaves `Uniq` evaluations attached to the source axiom set even though selection uses freshly copied clauses evaluated by the active HCB. Rust preserves this because it can affect later eval-order traversals of `state->axioms`, but a future cleanup could make the temporary ordering view explicit if reference tests show no caller depends on those source evaluations.
- `ProofStateInit` emits `DocClauseQuoteDefault(6, new, "eval")` before pushing the `DCCnfQuote` derivation. That helper clears `CPInputFormula` before its output-level gate, but assigns a fresh proof id only when the target level is reached, while the later derivation parent still points at the original source axiom. Rust preserves the input-marker clearing in both plain and documenting initialization and keeps proof-id mutation in the documenting wrapper; level-six executable coverage pins the eval quote and following id stream, but a future API should make the state transition independent of optional rendering.
- `document_processing` can change the selected clause's identifier before it is inserted into a processed set when OutputLevel reaches the proof-doc target. Rust mirrors that proof-id mutation only in the documenting wrapper; the output-only saturation/executable path emits the C OutputLevel 1 selected-clause text while preserving plain state ids. Keep the state-id/proof-id split explicit until executable proof-output tests decide how session-owned ids should be exposed to non-output callers.
- `check_watchlist` builds the packed FV query before calling `ClauseSubsumeOrderSortLits` and recomputing the candidate's standard weight. Rust sorts and weights before using the indexed query helper because the reusable indexed helpers own packing internally. This should be equivalent for order-insensitive FV features, but keep it as a reference-test target before changing or generalizing watchlist lookup.
- Dynamic `check_watchlist` interleaves mutation with global output and proof-documentation quotes for both removed watched clauses and the matching new clause. Rust now emits the represented proof-documentation quotes through the opt-in wrapper, emits the OutputLevel 1 watchlist-reduction message through both proof-documentation and output-only wrappers, and supported executable initialization/saturation threads the output stream and proof-documentation session through initial, selected, and generated-clause watchlist checks while maintaining explicitly supplied watchlist global indices.
- Dynamic `check_watchlist` deletes removed watched clauses from `state->wlindices` using `lambda_demod` before archiving them. Rust now deletes from the proof-state-owned watchlist `GlobalIndices` before archive movement in production, while lower-level helpers accept an explicit index borrow. Keep this ordering if clause identity is redesigned later.
- `ForwardModifyClause` accepts a `context_sr` flag but does not read it; contextual simplify-reflect is performed by `forward_contract_keep` after packing instead. Rust preserves this split in the staged clause-level wrapper; revisit the public helper boundaries again when generated-clause routing and set-level contraction share the wrapper.
- `cleanup_unprocessed_clauses` bases delete-bad cleanup on `ProofStateStorage`, a C byte estimate over selected clause sets and `TBStorage`. Rust now uses the C constant-memory `ClauseSetStorage` and `TBStorage` shapes, including FV-index storage, while demodulator `PDTreeStorage` remains zero until clause-set demodulator indexes are owned.
- `cleanup_unprocessed_clauses` interleaves queue mutation with progress writes to `GlobalOut`. Rust keeps the maintenance helper output-free and renders the same C-shaped branch messages from structured cleanup metadata in the saturation output bridge; keep that boundary unless later compatibility work proves callers depend on helper-local output timing.
- The cleanup orphan gate uses `ClauseSetDeleteOrphans`, whose C behavior depends on derivation entries holding live parent clause pointers. Rust's default path uses generation-qualified parent refs and constructs the full live/dead snapshot only when orphan or delete-bad cleanup can actually inspect it; a future proof-state arena should replace both raw pointers and repeated snapshots with validated stable handles.
- `insert_new_clauses` adds `state->tmp_store->members` and `state->tmp_store->literals` to generated counters before any contraction, deletion, replacement inference, or splitting. Rust preserves the initial snapshot and separately adds destructive equality-resolution and C-style controlled-splitting replacement counts to `generated_count`; revisit literal accounting after proof-output reference tests cover reused split-definition clauses.
- `ProcessClause` allocates `ClauseCopyDisjoint` immediately after variable normalization even for `SelectNoGeneration` and for clauses that later skip paramodulation. That apparently redundant copy interns renamed compound terms into the permanent bank and changes later entry-number ordering; Rust preserves it unconditionally. A cleaned inference API could allocate only for generators that consume the copy, but only outside drop-in mode because GEO288 traces show the allocation side effect is observable.
- The temporary-bank sweep threshold is a compile-time literal of 256 non-variable nodes and is checked only after the selected clause's disjoint copy has been freed. Rust preserves the threshold and phase. A future proof-session configuration could make scratch retention policy explicit after benchmarks show that changing collection frequency does not alter compatibility-visible resource behavior.
- `insert_new_clauses` handles `CPIsIRVictim` by calling `ForwardModifyClause` once with `FullRewrite`, ignoring that boolean return value, clearing `CPIsIRVictim`, and then running the normal `ForwardModifyClause` pass. Rust mirrors the double-modify shape; consider collapsing it only after inference-replacement tests prove the intermediate `CPLimitedRW` behavior is unobservable.
- `insert_new_clauses` emits `DocClauseQuoteDefault(6, handle, "eval")` after HCB evaluation and immediately before inserting each generated clause into `unprocessed`, so the proof-documentation layer can clear `CPInputFormula` and assign a fresh proof id to the generated clause. Rust keeps the plain helper's state ids unchanged and mirrors the proof-id mutation only in the documenting wrapper, including when `ProcessClause` owns the opt-in docs session; revisit the identity split after executable generated-clause proof-output tests are available.
- An empty clause returned from `insert_new_clauses` stops before `eval_clause_set`, so earlier survivors can remain in `eval_store` without HCB evaluations and later clauses can remain in `tmp_store`. Rust preserves this partial-state return because it is visible to the surrounding proof-search loop.
- Aggressive forward subsumption inside `insert_new_clauses` uses `aggressive_forward_subsumed_count`, not the processed-clause `proc_forward_subsumed_count`. Rust preserves the separate statistic; any future stats cleanup should keep reference-output compatibility in mind.
- The higher-order-only `NormalizeEquations` and `ClausePruneArgs` hooks inside `ForwardModifyClause` are now wired for represented clauses, and non-empty legacy KBO/LPO/KBO6 ordering now runs for first-order-shaped higher-order clauses and demodulators. The KBO6 backend has a visible LFHO DB/lambda/phony surface subset with ordinary deref propagation, local bound applied-variable expansion, and comparison-local weak-head beta dereferencing for `DEREF_ALWAYS`; the `ForwardModifyClause` path now also admits LFHO LPO4 visible surfaces through the bank-backed LPO4 comparison path when the live term bank is available. Proof-processing still guards full DB/lambda/phony generated/contraction surfaces until contraction-path normalization is integrated, and visible higher-order ordering surfaces outside the bank-backed LPO4/KBO6 paths remain staging diagnostics. Keep the HO forward-contraction gates separate until the ordering slice is complete.
- `ForwardModifyClause` proof-documentation side effects for represented rewrite steps, `DocClauseModificationDefault(..., inf_minimize, ...)` after superfluous-literal removal, `DocClauseModificationDefault(..., inf_condense, ...)` after successful condensation, and `DocClauseModificationDefault(..., inf_simplify_reflect, ...)` after each simplify-reflect literal removal are wired through the opt-in proof-documentation wrapper and supported executable saturation when proof output is enabled. Other modification documentation branches and higher-order normalization/pruning proof effects remain pending.
- `ClausePositiveSimplifyReflect` can be affected by the C process-global `StrongUnitForwardSubsumption` flag. Rust represents that as proof-control session configuration for forward subsumption and positive simplify-reflect; keep reference coverage around this path because it changes both the removed literal and the documented simplify-reflect partner.
- `prefer_initial_clauses` is implemented as a blanket negative priority offset on every active-HCB evaluation cell after evaluation. Rust preserves the numeric `-PrioLargestReasonable` rewrite; a later strategy API could represent this as a named priority tier once byte-for-byte heuristic behavior is no longer the immediate constraint.
- `ClauseSetScanAC` reports activation only when a commutativity axiom is detected; associativity-only scans still mark the signature associative but leave `control->ac_handling_active` false. Rust preserves this return-value split and now exposes the represented initialization scan/status output through an opt-in wrapper that is used by supported executable proof-state initialization, but a future API could separate "signature AC properties changed" from "commutativity activated AC handling" once broader callers are covered by reference tests.
- Dynamic `check_ac_status` prints the updated signature AC status and an activation message only when it turns AC handling on. Rust keeps the plain helper output-free, exposes opt-in proof-documentation and output-only wrappers for the represented OutputLevel stream, and supported executable saturation now threads the output/proof-documentation wrapper through selected-clause AC checks when proof output is enabled.
- C stores `GlobalIndices` directly in `ProofStateCell` as raw pointers tied to `state->signature`. Rust now stores both global-index owners directly in `ProofState`, but the indexes do not retain a signature borrow: arity-sensitive operations receive the live term-bank signature explicitly. Scoped access temporarily detaches the index values while a routine also needs `&mut ProofState`, avoiding a self-reference and preserving ordinary error-path restoration.
- `ProofStateResetProcessedSet` archives the original processed clause and requeues a flat copy with the same identifier and copied properties, so the same clause identifier can appear in both `archive` and `unprocessed`, and the requeued copy can still carry `CPIsProcessed`. Rust preserves this because it is visible to clause-set inspection; a later compatibility-relaxed API could make requeue identity and processed-state clearing explicit.
- `ProofStateResetProcessedSet` conditionally records `DCCnfEvalGC` on the archived original when proof-object GC selection is enabled and always emits a `move_eval` quote through the proof-documentation layer. Rust records both the optional GC-selection metadata and the unconditional `DCCnfQuote` on the requeued copy; the explicit proof-documentation wrapper now emits the represented `move_eval` quote, and the supported executable pre-saturation reset path uses that wrapper when proof output is enabled.
- Both reset and move-to-tmp paths delete `CPIsGlobalIndexed` clauses from `state->gindices` before moving them. Rust mirrors this through explicit index-borrow helpers driven by the long-lived index owned by `ProofState` in production.
- The `eval_clause_set` comment claims no side effects even though the function adds evaluation cells to every clause in `eval_store`. Rust documents the mutation explicitly.
- C evaluates clauses in place after inserting them into `eval_store`, so the set's evaluation trees do not receive entries until the clauses are later extracted and inserted into another set. Rust now mirrors the in-place mutation, temporarily owns the set to satisfy term-bank borrowing, and rebuilds its safe evaluation roots once after the batch. This preserves clause and evaluation-object order without turning the sparse store into an extract-and-append queue or transiently doubling its slot span.
- `insert_new_clauses` clears `CPIsOriented` both before literal selection/eval-store insertion and again when draining `eval_store` into `unprocessed`. Rust preserves the tail clearing so the eventual full helper can remain C-shaped; a later cleanup could collapse duplicate clearing only after selection and proof-output tests prove it unobservable.
- The `insert_new_clauses` admission step stores `proc_non_trivial_count` in each clause's `create_date`. Rust currently has unsigned proof-state counters and a signed C-shaped clause date field, so the conversion saturates at `i64::MAX`; revisit the type split after end-to-end search/reference tests determine whether date overflow behavior needs exact C compatibility.
- `select_on_proc_only` bypasses the full `DoLiteralSelection` wrapper and clears only selected literal flags before eval-store insertion. Rust preserves this flag-level behavior; a later API could make the option name/phase split clearer without changing compatibility defaults.
- C treats `DoLiteralSelection` as infallible after option parsing. Rust now has full selector-body coverage for the C name table; only low-level direct calls can still report a diagnostic when a banked/ordering-dependent selector is invoked without the required term bank or proof-control OCB.
- `insert_new_clauses` destructive equality resolution (`ClauseERNormalizeVar`) and controlled splitting (`ControlledClauseSplit`) both mutate `tmp_store` and generated counters when they replace a generated clause. Rust now ports the bank-aware single-MGU destructive equality-resolution path plus fresh and non-fresh controlled splitting, including arity-zero fresh and reusable non-fresh split-definition formula archive parents and opt-in split proof-documentation output on represented clauses; lower-level `DefStore` construction remains separate from the executable saturation proof-documentation session.
- `replacing_inferences` checks higher-order immediate clausification before destructive equality resolution and splitting, but `ImmediateClausification` itself is a narrow `EqnIsClausifiable` gate; non-clausifiable higher-order clauses continue through the ordinary replacement branches. Rust preserves that no-op fallthrough and now runs the C-shaped `WFormulaOfClause`/`FormulaSet` simplification, definition-introduction, proof-documenting wrapped-CNF, and final selected-clause `DCDynamicCNF` parent route for clausifiable selected clauses.
- `replacing_inferences` sets `pclause->clause = NULL`, unpacks the `FVPackedClause_p`, and then delegates to `insert_new_clauses` whenever immediate clausification, destructive equality resolution, or splitting replaces the selected clause. Rust consumes the owned `FvPackedClause` and reports that state with `ReplacingInferenceOutcome`; replace this with stable clause handles once the selected-clause processing loop owns C-shaped packed-clause aliases.
- `replacing_inferences` performs destructive equality resolution when `er_varlit_destructive` is enabled even if `er_aggressive` is disabled. Rust preserves that separate gate; avoid collapsing it with generated-clause aggressive ER unless reference tests prove the phase distinction is unobservable.
- `ProcessClause` normalizes selected-clause variables with `state->freshvars`, which is separate from but shadow-paired with `state->terms->vars`. Rust now mirrors that owner split; keep the separation because using the term bank's own `VarBank` for normalization can self-bind variables and make dereferencing non-terminating.
- `ClauseSetIndexedInsert` receives the same packed-clause alias used by forward contraction and later unpacks it after processed-set insertion. Rust currently inserts an owned clause into the target set and rebuilds any FV index from that owned value; replace this with stable selected-clause handles when the full processed-clause loop is represented.
- `ProcessClause` deletes the exact `arch_copy` pointer if forward contraction consumes a selected clause after proof-object GC archive copying. Rust currently deletes the archived copy by identifier because archive entries are owned values; replace this with stable archive handles if duplicate archived identifiers become observable.
- The backward simplification calls inside `ProcessClause` use `state->gindices.bw_rw_index` as the sole discovery source when configured, delete matched processed clauses from `state->gindices`, emit proof-documentation quotes, and then either archive dead originals or move quoted flat copies into `tmp_store`. Although nearby C comments mention killing children, the current removal bodies archive or requeue the affected clauses without traversing child links. Rust preserves the authoritative-index/plain-fallback split, local set/archive/tmp-store movement and statistics, deletion through explicit index borrows from the state-owned global index, and represented backward-subsumption and simplifiable-movement quotes through opt-in docs wrappers.
- `generate_new_clauses` begins with `VarBankSetVCountsToUsed(state->terms->vars)` before any generator runs, advancing live term-bank per-sort reuse counters while separate reusable `state->freshvars` counters are still reset inside lower-level generators. Rust now mirrors the live-bank pre-seeding at the staged helper boundary and keeps short-lived normalization banks for helpers that cannot yet borrow proof-state-owned `freshvars`; make these fresh-variable counter boundaries explicit in a later proof-session owner before trying to simplify variable allocation.
- `generate_new_clauses` calls higher-order generation unconditionally before the first-order generators. Rust now runs the represented ArgCong, NegExt, PosExt, inverse-recognition, indexed ExtSup/ExtEqRes/ExtEqFact, Leibniz-elimination, primitive-enumeration, and choice-instantiation branches before first-order generators; production proof control supplies the extension indexes owned by `ProofState`, while unindexed library entry points still diagnose strategies that require them.
- `ProcessClause` always reaches `generate_new_clauses` unless the selected literal strategy is `NoGeneration`. Rust now supports first-order and higher-order generation in that path, including the complete checked-C `ComputeHOInferences` dispatcher and state-owned indexed paramodulation. Do not describe already-wired higher-order dispatcher branches as pending.
- C does not insert a blanket higher-order guard before the ordinary equality factoring, equality resolution, disequality decomposition, or paramodulation calls in `generate_new_clauses`; the lower helpers and global `problemType` decide what higher-order behavior is legal. Rust currently mirrors that ordering but keeps first-order-shaped KBO6 guards around paramodulation until LFHO ordering and CSU enumeration are fully ported.
- C's `ComputeHOInferences` uses `neg_ext` as the gate for both negative and positive extensionality, so a strategy that sets only `pos_ext` does not reach `ComputePosExt` in the checked source. Rust mirrors that behavior by preserving the `pos_ext`-alone no-op and running represented positive extensionality only when the C gate would make it observable; revisit it only after higher-order strategy/reference traces can distinguish compatibility from an accidental C option bug.
- `simplify_watchlist` prefers `state->wlindices.bw_rw_index` when available and does not fall back to a plain scan if that index exists but is stale or incomplete. Rust preserves this with the state-owned watchlist `GlobalIndices`, while still falling back to the owned watchlist scan when no backward-rewrite index is configured. Keep the authoritative-index behavior only for compatibility; a later debug/session API could validate watchlist/index consistency before search.
- `simplify_watchlist` emits proof-documentation output for minimization and simplification moves. Rust now exposes those represented rewrite/minimize quotes through an opt-in documenting wrapper and threads that wrapper through opt-in `ProcessClause` documentation while keeping the plain helpers output-free; supported executable initialization/saturation proof-session ownership is integrated for the represented paths.
- `Saturate` compares signed `generated_limit` and `tb_insert_limit` against unsigned C counters, so negative limits become very large unsigned sentinels, and the generated counter expression can wrap if backward-rewritten clauses exceed generated clauses. Rust preserves this through explicit helper casts and wrapping subtraction; revisit only with reference tests if a higher-level limit API wants conventional signed sentinel semantics.
- C uses watchlist pointer presence to stop saturation once an active watchlist becomes empty. Rust proof states allocate an empty optional watchlist by default, so the port adds an explicit activation bit set by `ProofStateLoadWatchlist`; keep this compatibility shim until executable watchlist source ownership can represent "no watchlist" and "active empty watchlist" without ambiguity.
- `Saturate` increments SAT-check thresholds after each completed `SATCheck`, including repeated size-threshold catch-up and term-bank insertion threshold doubling. `SATCheck` first runs `ForwardContractSetReweight` when unprocessed normalization is enabled; an empty clause found there returns before `SatClauseSetCheckUnsat`, so C records the proof root but emits no SAT-solver UNSAT comment and does not update solver-result counters. Rust now distinguishes that preprocessing refutation from solver-reported SATCheck UNSAT while preserving the shared extraction-root path and threshold scheduling; revisit if exact PicoSAT decision-limit behavior changes when the external solver is wired in.
- C pushes extraction roots from semantically false `ProcessClause` answers, empty replacement-inference results, generated empty clauses, cleanup-time forward contraction, and SATCheck before returning proof-success roots. Rust now records represented clause roots for those ported proof-control paths at the same layer: `ProcessClause` records answer, replacement, and generated-empty roots directly, while `Saturate` records cleanup and SATCheck roots. Answer-limit roots are recorded after answer-literal evaluation and non-returning answer roots are snapshotted after processed-clause insertion. Mixed formula roots still need the broader proof-documentation owner.
- C stores raw clause pointers in `extract_roots`, so roots can reflect later in-place clause mutation. Rust currently stores owned clause snapshots; keep this compatibility boundary under reference tests and consider stable clause handles before adding formula-side or long-lived proof-object extraction.
- The `insert_new_clauses` eval-store drain emits `DocClauseQuoteDefault(..., "eval")` in C. Rust now exposes the represented quote through the opt-in generated-clause documentation wrapper, threads it through opt-in `ProcessClause` documentation, and uses the same session from supported executable saturation when proof output is enabled.

### Porting Focus

- Keep the generated public-surface inventory above in sync with the source, but treat this manual section as the place for compatibility judgments.
- Before replacing C idioms with safer Rust abstractions, identify whether callers depend on object identity, global state, allocation reuse, or fatal-error behavior.
- If behavior is unclear, prefer matching the C source first and adding Rust-side tests around the observed C behavior.
